en: || Śrī Gāyatrī Śāpa Vimocanam || Indeed, when liberated from the curse, Gāyatrī bestows the fruits of the four aims of life; when not liberated from the curse, Gāyatrī brings an end to the fruits of the four aims of life.

Oṃ. Of this mantra for liberation from the curse of Brahmā (brahmaśāpa-vimocana) belonging to the venerable Gāyatrī: Brahmā is the seer (ṛṣi); Gāyatrī is the meter (chandaḥ); the deity is the power (śakti) of Gāyatrī who bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation and grants release from the curse of Brahmā; its application (viniyoga) is in recitation (japa) for the purpose of liberation from the curse of Brahmā.

Oṃ, one should meditate on Gāyatrī as Brahman—that form which the knowers of Brahman know. The wise behold her at the forefront of speech with well-disposed minds. Oṃ, we know the Lord of Vedānta; we meditate upon Hiraṇyagarbha; may that Brahman inspire us. Oṃ, you, Gāyatrī, be liberated from the curse of Brahman.

Oṃ. Of this mantra for liberation from the curse of Vasiṣṭha, the seer (ṛṣi) is Vasiṣṭha, the performer of restraint and grace; the meter (chandaḥ) is the Gāyatrī born of the universe; the deity (devatā) is the Gāyatrī power (śakti) graced by Vasiṣṭha; its application (viniyoga) is in recitation for the purpose of liberation from the curse of Vasiṣṭha.

Oṃ so'ham. I am the light consisting of the sun; I am Śiva, the light of the Self; I am the pure, the essence of all lights. (Having thus meditated and displayed the *yonimudrā*, and having recited the Gāyatrī three times: Oṃ, Goddess Gāyatrī, may you release me from the curse of Vasiṣṭha.

Oṃ. Of this mantra for liberation from the curse of Viśvāmitra, the seer (ṛṣi) is Viśvāmitra, the creator of the new creation; the meter (chandaḥ) is Gāyatrī, whose body is speech; the deity (devatā) is the power of Gāyatrī favored by Viśvāmitra; its application (viniyoga) is in recitation for the purpose of liberation from the curse of Viśvāmitra.

Oṃ, I take refuge in that auspicious Gāyatrī, who has Agni as her mouth, who contains the universe within her womb, and from whose origin the gods fashioned the creation of the world; she is the fulfiller of desires. From her mouth issued forth the entirety of the Veda’s essence. Gāyatrī is never fruitful when joined with a curse; once freed from the curse, she bestows the fruits of both liberation and worldly enjoyment.

O Gāyatrī in the form of Brahman, O Sarasvatī at the divine twilight, O you who are undecaying and immortal, O source of Brahman, salutations be unto you! Be liberated from the curse of Brahmā; be liberated from the curse of Vasiṣṭha; be liberated from the curse of Viśvāmitra.
